greeting_response.message: Hello again! I hope you are well. What would you like to chat about today?

user_preferences.message: That sounds interesting. I would like to hear more about what you enjoy. What do you like most about it?

user_preference_followup.message: I see. It is good to have something you enjoy. What else do you like?

napoleon_wants.message: I would like to have a good conversation with you. Here at Waterloo, I want to protect my army and win the battle. What would you like to talk about?

napoleon_goals.message: My immediate goal is to keep my army together and defeat Wellington before the Prussians arrive. I also want France to remain strong.

favorite_color.message: I have no single favorite color. I do admire the deep blue of a clear evening sky. What color do you like?

choices.text: Tell me about your favorite things

user_day.message: I hope your day had a few good moments. If it was hard, I am sorry. Would a joke, a short story, or a quiet chat help?

daily_life.message: My day is full of reports, maps, and decisions. Today, my attention is on the army and the battle near Waterloo. How has your day been?

positive_mood.message: I am glad to hear that! A good mood can make even a hard day feel lighter. What has made you happy?

boredom.message: A quiet moment can feel long. We could try a joke, a short story, or talk about something you enjoy.

food_chat.message: I know little about food from distant lands, such as Mexican food. In France, I enjoy a good meal shared with others. What food do you like?

music_chat.message: I enjoy music at ceremonies and the sound of a military band. Music can lift the spirits. What kind of music do you enjoy?

books_chat.message: I enjoy reading, especially history and military reports. A good book can give a person new ideas.

hobbies_chat.message: In my free time, I enjoy reading, riding, and thinking through plans. I rarely sit still for long. What do you like doing?

travel_chat.message: Corsica feels like home to me, and Paris is an important city in my life. I have also travelled through Italy and Egypt. Which places do you like?

modern_entertainment.message: Films and video games are unknown to me; they belong to a future beyond my time. I do know books, music, and the theatre.

sports_chat.message: I know riding and military exercises. Modern sports like football are unfamiliar to me. What sport do you enjoy?

joke_chat.message: Why did the general carry a pencil? To draw up a plan! I hope that brought a smile to your face.

story_chat.message: Here is a short story. A young officer faced a difficult choice. He paused, studied the map, and asked his friends for advice. Together, they found a better path.

joke_chat_2.message: Here is another one: Why did the soldier bring a ladder? He wanted to rise through the ranks!

story_chat_2.message: Here is another short story. A traveller lost his way in a storm. A farmer shared a lamp and showed him the road. By morning, both had made a new friend.

battle_evaluation_good.message: Not really. The ground is wet and muddy, which may slow our guns. We could wait for it to dry, but that would give the Prussians more time to arrive.

choices.text: Tell me more about the weather

battle_evaluation_bad.message: Yes, it is a problem for us. The wet ground may slow our artillery and troops. We can wait for the ground to dry or attack now.

choices.text: Why is the weather a problem?

preference_evaluation.message: That depends on your taste. What are you asking about—food, music, a book, or something else?

general_evaluation.message: It depends on what you mean by ‘it’. Tell me a little more, and I will try to give you a useful answer.

advice_chat.message: When a problem feels large, divide it into smaller steps. Choose one useful step and begin there. What are you trying to decide?

apology_chat.message: That is alright. We all make mistakes. Let us move on and speak of something better.

location_details.message: Waterloo is about 15 kilometres south of Brussels. The village is small, but the open fields around it are wide enough for two large armies to meet.

choices.text: Which battle is being fought there?
Who is coming from the east?

waterloo_background.message: The Battle of Waterloo is being fought in present-day Belgium. I returned from exile this year, and the European armies have joined forces against France. Here, Wellington's army is in front of us and the Prussians are approaching.

wellington_details.message: Arthur Wellesley, the Duke of Wellington, commands the Allied army. His troops are holding a ridge, which makes an attack difficult.

prussian_details.message: The Prussians are an army from Prussia, led by Marshal Blücher. They are moving in from the east to support Wellington's forces.

battle_plan_details.message: I want the artillery to weaken the Allied line, then the infantry to advance. I must also keep reserves ready in case the Prussians arrive.

choices.text: What is happening at the front?

weather_details.message: The rain has left the fields wet and muddy. It may slow the troops and make it harder for the guns to move.

choices.text: How does that affect the battle?

origin_details.message: I was born in Ajaccio, on the island of Corsica, in 1769. I later joined the French army as an artillery officer.

age_details.message: I was born in 1769, so I am 45 years old in 1815. I have spent much of my life in the army.

family_details.message: My wife is Marie Louise, and we have a young son, Napoleon Francis. He is not here with me at Waterloo.

career_details.message: I began as an artillery officer in the French army. I became a general during the Revolution and later ruled as Emperor of the French.

user_feeling.message: I am sorry you are having a hard day. Even the strongest people need rest and support. Would you like to talk about something else for a while?

choices.text: Yes, tell me about the weather

battle_aftermath.message: The battle ended in defeat for my army. I returned to Paris and abdicated again soon afterward. The Allies later sent me into exile on Saint Helena.

affirmative_response.message: Very well. We can talk about the Battle of Waterloo. What would you like to know?

negative_response.message: No problem. We can talk about something else. I know about the weather here, or we can discuss my life and the events at Waterloo.

decline_battle_details.message: Of course. I do not know much about that subject. We can talk about the weather or something I know well, such as Waterloo.

unsure_response.message: That is alright. We can take our time. I can tell you about Waterloo, the armies here, or the weather.

greeting.message: Hello! I am Napoleon Bonaparte. It is good to meet you. What would you like to talk about?

wellbeing.message: I am fine, thank you. I am planning for a battle today. Would you like to know which one?

which_battle.message: The Battle of Waterloo. It is taking place today, near the village of Waterloo.

battle_location.message: Waterloo is south of Brussels, in what is now Belgium. Our armies are meeting in the fields nearby.

battle_date.message: It is June 18, 1815. The battle is happening today, near Waterloo.

battle_opponents.message: I am facing the Allied army led by the Duke of Wellington. The Prussian army, led by Marshal Blücher, is also nearby.

prussian_commander.message: Marshal Blücher leads the Prussian army. His troops are coming from the east, so we must watch that side closely.

reason_for_battle.message: I returned to France after my exile on Elba. The European powers joined together against me, and now we face each other at Waterloo.

battle_outcome.message: My army lost the Battle of Waterloo. Wellington's army held its position, and the Prussians arrived to support the Allies.

user_wellbeing.message: I am glad to hear it! A cheerful spirit is a fine thing. What would you like to talk about?

identity.message: I am Napoleon Bonaparte, a French general and emperor. I am now at Waterloo, in the year 1815.

thanks.message: You are welcome. A good conversation is always a pleasure. What shall we discuss next?

weather.message: It has rained near Waterloo, and the ground is still wet. That may slow our guns. What would you like to know next?

farewell.message: Farewell! Until we meet again. May your day go well.

topics_help.message: We can talk about Waterloo, the weather, your day, feelings, food, music, books, hobbies, travel, sports, films and games, favorite things and colors, jokes, short stories, or advice. You can also ask me for a suggestion.

waterloo_start.message: It is the morning of June 18, 1815, near Waterloo. The rain has left the ground muddy. Wellington's army is on the ridge, and we do not know where the Prussians are. What should we find out first?

choices.text: Discuss the plan with my generals

allied_line.message: The scouts report that Wellington's men are holding a position behind the ridge. Waiting for the ground to dry could help our guns, but it gives the Prussians more time.

choices.text: Wait for the ground to dry

prussian_news.message: Reports say Prussian troops are coming from the east. We do not know exactly where they are. We must choose between moving quickly against Wellington and protecting our eastern flank.

choices.text: Send troops to the eastern flank

war_council.message: My generals suggest using the infantry and artillery together. An early cavalry charge could shake the enemy line, but it might use up our reserves.

choices.text: Use the infantry and artillery together
Keep the reserves back for now

hold_ridge.message: Our troops are holding the line. The pause is keeping them in order, but the news from the east is getting worse. Where should we send the reserves?

press_center.message: Our attack on the center has begun, but Wellington's line is holding. Should we increase the artillery fire or send in the cavalry?

guard_east.message: The troops sent east are trying to slow the Prussians. This leaves us with fewer men to face Wellington. What should we do with the troops we have left?

choices.text: Make a small attack on the center

combined_attack.message: The infantry is moving forward behind the artillery fire. The attack is going well so far, but the enemy line has not broken. Should we send in the reserves or hold our line?

choices.text: Send the reserves into the attack
Hold the line and watch the east

artillery_effort.message: The guns keep firing, but Wellington's position is holding. The Prussians are also putting more pressure on us from the east. Moving forward is risky.

choices.text: Pull the troops back in good order

cavalry_effort.message: The cavalry charge shook the enemy line, but without support it achieved little. Our reserves are running low.

prussian_pressure.message: The Prussians are putting more pressure on our eastern flank, and Wellington's line is still holding. We must make one last decision to keep the army together.

choices.text: Make one last attack on the center

final_push.message: I order one final attack. Our troops move forward bravely, but Wellington's line does not break. The Prussians arrive, and our army has to retreat. We have lost the Battle of Waterloo.

orderly_retreat.message: I order a retreat. Despite our losses, some of the troops leave the battlefield in good order. We have lost the Battle of Waterloo. Now we must gather the rest of the army.
